title: Adaptive probe calibration and shadow autoscaler postmortem
creator: Ava Martinez
description: After a production capacity event on 2025-10-31 we observed an increased incidence of scale-downs driven by noisy probe samples that caused downstream cold-start spikes and elevated tail latency. A shadow autoscaler experiment we had running flagged an increased false-negative rate but our live HPA/KEDA config still applied aggressive downscaling. This ticket captures the postmortem, the calibration changes we implemented (adaptive probe smoothing + gated probe gating), and the rollout/runbook updates to prevent regressions.
impact: Across two regions we saw sustained 15–25% higher p99 latency for synchronous generation endpoints during the 3-hour window. No customer data lost, but several high-throughput customers experienced transient request errors due to worker churn and cold-start penalties. SLO breach for latency was narrowly avoided; error-rate stayed within SLO but customer experience degraded.
timeline: 2025-10-31 02:13 UTC: Unusual traffic pattern (high variance bursts) begins in us-west-2. Alert: queue depth increased.
2025-10-31 02:21 UTC: KEDA scaled down a subset of pods based on 95th percentile probe crossing the downthreshold. Observed oscillatory decisions across 3 minutes.
2025-10-31 02:24 UTC: p95/p99 latency spikes observed. On-call paged.
root_cause: The primary root cause was probe sampling aliasing where short, high-variance bursts contaminated the percentile window used by KEDA/HPA. Our existing downscale gating used a fixed percentile and window which made it sensitive to bursty traffic. The shadow autoscaler (which had been configured with different smoothing) showed fewer false-down decisions but its outputs were only advisory. A recent config merge reduced the probe smoothing time constant to improve responsiveness, which unintentionally increased false positives for downscales during this bursty workload.
decision_log: We reverted the recent smoothing time-constant reduction (PR #5123) to restore previous stability while longer-term measures are implemented. Decision approved by on-call and infra leads.

Add an adaptive smoothing algorithm that grows the smoothing window proportionally to observed signal variance; trade-off: slightly slower scale-down responsiveness during bursty patterns but substantially fewer false-downs.
Enable probe gating: scale-down is only allowed when both smoothed probe and short-window median agree. This trades a small increase in cost for higher reliability.
Roll out shadow autoscaler in advisory mode to 100% of clusters so we can compare decisions without affecting production during the tuning phase.
Update alerting to include a 'probe noise' signal so SREs are paged when probe variance exceeds historical baseline.
